newsitem.title: LATVIA: Nomura sees better Lithuanian bank returns.
newsitem.headline: Nomura sees better Lithuanian bank returns.

text.p: Investment house Nomura said on Thursday it preferred Lithuanian bank stocks for better returns in 1997 than those in Estonia, which have seen a strong rally.
Nomura bank analyst Mike Wheelhouse recommended leading Lithuanian bank Vilnius Bank and also Ukio Bankas.

Wheelhouse said Estonian banks had been re-rated over the past 12 months due to earnings momentum and speculative buying after Swedish Swedbank bought a stake in second-largest Estonian bank, Savings Bank.

"Lithuanian bank shares look far more promising, both from a valuation perspective and in view of the growth prospects open to the private sector institutions following the crisis of confidence in the large public sector banks," Wheelhouse said.
Wheelhouse said Vilnius Bank was his top recommendation with a 1997 price/earnings ratio expected at 5.20 and 4.01 in 1998.
He also recommended Ukio Bankas, with P/Es in 1997 of 3.50 and 2.26 in 1996. This compared with a forecast sector average for central Europe of 6.54 in 1997 and 5.45 in 1998.
Wheelhouse also recommended buys in Estonia's top bank Hansapank, Forekspank and Savings Bank and a hold on Union Bank.
He also said buy Lithuania's second largest bank Hermis Bank as well as Latvia's leading bank Unibanka.
He said Unibanka should perform well as it gets set to launch a GDR and that a proposed merger with Zemes Bank would be well received.
But he said Unibanka needed a resurgence in growth to offset a fall in interest spreads.
